chapter: Boston, Buffalo and finding a style
title: A white-owned club with a mixed audience and no racial problems
summary: The Silver Grill was white-owned with a mixed clientele and no problems, which Crouch calls unusual for 1935; Boston was the same.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Who owned the Silver Grill? I mean, was it -- what kind of a place was it?
It was -- I forget the manager's name. So long ago, of course, you know.
Was this, was it a -- was this a Negro club or white club?
Yeah. It was owned by whites.
Oh, it was a mixed clientele?
And there was no -- there were no problems?
There was no -- you didn't have any problem with fraternizing with the --
Even when I went to Boston and I played there, there was no problems.
Well, that's very, because, you know, a lot of people have told me that even in New York City they ran into a whole lot of stuff in a lot of places where you couldn't --
